scientific_question: On two exact original publicly observed action environments, does legitimate past public history improve strictly proper categorical next-complete-public outcome log score over a fully fitted same-information exact-full-current Bayesian count baseline?
action_policy: Existing MR34E source-blind random.Random(1000003*seed+337).randrange(actions); identical exploration opportunity across both fitted arms
prediction_target: Entire exact next original public observation sha256 digest, NOT segmented change indicator; source full-public preaction SHA and action used as memoryless context; native previous two true public observation/action SHA pairs only for history model
models: train-only exact full current public+action Dirichlet-multinomial with empirical global prior
same fitted current prediction with extra conditional previous 2 original-public observations/actions backoff
evaluation: Strictly proper full categorical log score in nats per transition and aggregate mean per independent reset seed; paired memoryless minus history scores; 1000 deterministic cluster bootstrap resamples at source seed level (not per step), 95% percentile interval
advance_boundary: Development informational support only when lower 95% cluster-bootstrapped difference bound positive on BOTH sources and history contexts have repeats in public TRAIN. Even a positive is NOT P0FC1 science acceptance without independently trained competent full-current recurrent/Bayesian/symbolic controls, native learning, action outcome benefit, true restart, independent held source first-use and all-in resources.
negative_rule: If history does not beat exact full-current fit, retain negative for this exact context model/finite exploration. If held history coverage zero, label inadequate support; neither implies no other learnable history mechanism.
